title.title: The Correspondence of Esther Roberts Hunt Collins

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: In love and affection I salute thee with a few lines & inform that I have received two letters from the, which were truly acceptable, as was the accounts therein contained. I desire thee to continue me so much under thy motive as to write when there is time. We have been favored with health and many blessings, which I desire to be truly thankful for. Yet I feel so many cumbering hindering things that I fear that I shall never attain to what my soul desireth. We have been visited by a number of valuable friends, Issac Everett & several by appointment from the yearly-meeting. Joshua Evans in the 9th month, whose labor was truly acceptable to a number. Ann Jessop & Lydia Hyatt from Carolina & as soon as they were gone. Jarvice Johnson from Europe with his companion Alexander Wilson & while they were here. Susannah Hollinsworth & Lydia from the Eastern shore in Maryland.
The women have it in their prospect to visit all the families belonging to friends, & are now engaged in that service, & have gone through the monthly meeting of Westland except some outskirts.
That it seems comparatively speaking that we are lug about, to try a little longer weather there will be any fruit. Oh, may a blessing attend the abundant labors that have been bestowed.

About two months ago brother Robert’s two oldest sons & their wives came out here & in a little while after their son Samuel. Joshua with wife & two children have lived in our shop until about a week ago. They have gone to live at the sawmill he has bought of James French and from accounts I am inclined to think its low time with Robert. He informed me that he has a prospect of coming out here in the spring, & is unsettled having a home to seek being disappointed in his prospects & this winter is keeping school.
Oh, may we be each of us directed by best wisdom, that we may have a staff to lean upon. I feel a need of it.

postscript.p: The remembrance of being amongst you my dear friends, is often very fresh in my mind, & my heart is often affected with being so far separated from you, & as it were in the wilderness, where I feel a fear that I shall fall a prey. The many cumbering hindering things are too much. Oh, may help be afforded that my way may be made plain before me; feeling myself so deficient of being what I ought to be & therefore unified to do my duty in regard of myself & those under my care. The children are grown more out of my arms, though not out of a painful concern for them, & believe there is much due to them of right education wherein I feel so deficient.
I don’t wish to tire thee with my poor scribble therefore conclude with love to thee wife & children with the rest of my friends & relations
